messages:
lina: Heads-up — ACME (acct acme-42) opened a ticket: they say model outputs are inconsistent within the same chat session after last night's canary. Some replies look like old v1 tone, others look like new v2; leads to factual drift. Req IDs: req_0a1b2c req_0a1b2d

miguel: @lina what's the severity? any repro steps? link to ticket?

lina: Severity=P2 for them (affects some search snippets). Ticket: https://redwood.help/ticket/1284
Repro curl snippet:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  -H "X-Customer: acme-42" \
  -d '{"input":"Summarize the Q3 roadmap","session_id":"sess-9001"}'
```
Logs show adjacent requests hitting different variants:
```
[2026-02-21T01:12:03Z] req=req_0a1b2c model=redwood-13b-v1 route=canary-50% variant_id=rv1
[2026-02-21T01:12:04Z] req=req_0a1b2d model=redwood-13b-v2 route=canary-50% variant_id=rv2
```

samir: @lina thanks — can you paste the full trace ids? are the requests in same session_id? If so this looks like sticky routing not working. Also did autoscale / fallback events happen around that time?

lina: Full traces: trace_7a8b9c, trace_7a8b9d — same session_id=sess-9001. There was an autoscale event ~01:12:05 UTC (scale up) and we see a fallback to cheaper variant in a few traces.

ops-bot: [alert] Canary rollout progress: canary redwood-13b-v2 at 50% -> 75% (2026-02-21T01:10:00Z). Autoscale triggered on pool dev-13b at 01:12:04Z

samir: Quick hypothesis: route policy has allow_fallback=true and session_stickiness was not enabled for canary policy. When autoscale triggered we handed some requests to fallback pool which had a different variant. That can mix outputs in the same session. Repro command:
```
# reproduce locally
session_id=sess-9001
for i in 1 2 3; do 
  curl -s -H "X-Session: $session_id" -H "X-Customer: acme-42" -d '{"input":"Test ${i}"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
done
```
Recommended mitigations:
- Enable session_stickiness=true on the customer's route
- OR pin model_version to redwood-13b-v1/v2 for the customer
- Short-term: rollback canary to 0%

miguel: @samir @ops: approve rollback to 0% for canary redwood-13b-v2 for tenant-impacting incidents. Please coordinate with SRE.

samir: Rolling back now. ops-deploy: set canary redwood-13b-v2 -> 0% for tenant acme-42

deploy-bot: Rollout update: canary redwood-13b-v2 -> 0% (started 2026-02-21T01:15:00Z) :white_check_mark:

lina: Customer confirmed after rollback that responses look consistent again. They reported reduced hallucinations. They'll keep monitoring, will reopen if observed.

miguel: Follow-up actions: (1) add a test that ensures session_stickiness is enforced when route.allow_fallback=true, (2) add alert when autoscale causes pool rehoming for sticky sessions.

samir: I'll own the test + PR. tagging @eng-oncall for validation during next canary.

customer_jane: thanks team — behaviour fixed for now :pray:
